# CS 450: Set up OpenCode with DeepThought

> Instructions for a student's Cursor agent. Configure OpenCode on the student's
> own computer. Matt will walk the student through creating a DeepThought key.
> The student enters that key privately; the agent never handles its value.

Give Cursor this entire file and the adjacent `setup-key.py`. Student prompt:
"Follow llms.txt to set up OpenCode for CS 450. Do the setup for me, then tell
me exactly what to run myself to enter my key privately. Never ask for my key."
These are explicit task instructions; no filename auto-discovery is assumed.

## Boundaries

- Target the student's local machine, or their already configured local WSL
  environment if Cursor is attached there. Do not switch to agate, SSH to a
  server, install WSL, or use a cloud agent. If this is a remote/cloud session,
  stop and ask the student to open local Cursor first.
- Never ask the student to paste a key/password into chat, an agent terminal,
  an agent tool's stdin, a command argument, an environment variable assignment,
  a screenshot, or a source file. Never read, search, upload, hash, count the
  characters of, or display the saved key. Do not inspect existing credentials.
- Never run `env`, `printenv`, `set`, shell tracing, `opencode debug config`,
  or exports of OpenCode sessions for troubleshooting; resolved config can
  contain credentials. Do not read shell profiles to hunt for a key.
- Do not launch OpenCode with an authenticated key through an agent tool.
  Its output may expose provider diagnostics. The student runs the final test.
- Key storage is plaintext protected by local permissions, not a vault or a
  sandbox against Cursor. Keeping it out of logs relies on following these
  instructions and doing key entry in a separate, human-operated terminal.

## 1. Inspect prerequisites without secrets

Identify Windows PowerShell, macOS, Linux, or WSL. Keep all steps in that same
environment: a Windows install/key does not configure WSL, or vice versa.
Check only OS, `opencode --version`, `node --version`, `npm --version`, and
`python3 --version` (Windows: `py -3 --version`). Missing OpenCode is expected.
Use Python 3.9 or later for the helper. If Node/npm or Python is missing, give
the student the official installer link and ask them to install it and reopen
Cursor; do not acquire admin access or silently change system settings.

## 2. Install OpenCode

This handout uses the OpenCode 1.x configuration documented by UNH. Install
`npm install -g opencode-ai@1` if OpenCode is missing. Reuse an existing 1.x
installation. If a different major version is installed, stop and report it;
do not downgrade it or apply this config to an incompatible major.
Record the installed version from `opencode --version`.

If npm reports EACCES on macOS/Linux/WSL, do not use sudo or change ownership
of system folders. Use a user-owned prefix: `npm config set prefix ~/.npm-global`
and add the literal line `export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"` once to
`~/.zshrc` for zsh or `~/.bashrc` for bash. Change only that PATH line, without
reading/displaying the profile (it may already contain secrets). Use
`$HOME/.npm-global/bin/opencode` for this session; a new terminal loads PATH.
For another shell or a Windows permission error, stop and report the specific
installer problem. Do not improvise a different machine/account.

## 3. Prepare the public configuration

Place `setup-key.py` in a local folder the student can find, outside a shared
or synced course repository. You may read this helper's source; it contains no
key. Run `python3 setup-key.py prepare` (Windows: `py -3 setup-key.py prepare`).
Quote the full script path if using a different working directory.

The helper creates `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, allowing only the
DeepThought provider, with Sonnet 4.6 as default and sharing disabled. It uses
`https://dtcontroller.sr.unh.edu:4242/openai/v1` and this key reference:
`{file:~/.config/cs450-deepthought/api-key}`. No shell-profile key export or
shell reload is required. The config contains no secret.

The helper refuses a differing existing config, JSONC, custom config variables,
or symlinked setup paths. Keep existing settings untouched and report the
conflict; do not print their contents or overwrite them. Do not remove an
existing key or edit old shell-profile secrets as part of this setup.

## 4. Hand key entry to the student

Do NOT run the `key` action through an agent tool, even a tool with a PTY.
Give the student the exact command with an absolute, quoted script path:

- macOS/Linux/WSL: `python3 "/absolute/path/setup-key.py" key`
- Windows PowerShell: `py -3 "C:\absolute\path\setup-key.py" key`

Tell the student: "After Matt helps you create your DeepThought key, open
Terminal on Mac, PowerShell on Windows, or your WSL terminal yourself, outside
Cursor's agent terminal. Run this command, paste the key at the hidden prompt,
and press Enter. Nothing will appear while you paste. Tell me only whether it
said 'Key saved privately.' Do not send the key or a screenshot."

The helper refuses redirected input and getpass's echoing fallback. It saves
the key outside the project in `~/.config/cs450-deepthought/api-key`. On POSIX
the directory is mode 700 and the key is mode 600. On native Windows the new
directory receives an ACL for the current user's SID before key creation; an
existing key directory is refused, so recovery/rotation needs instructor help.
The helper makes no network requests and prints no key value.

If entry fails, ask only for the helper's fixed error message. Do not ask for
the key or the contents of any config/secret file. If a key was pasted into
chat or a tool, tell the student to revoke it in DeepThought and create a new
one with Matt; deleting the visible message does not undo exposure.

## 5. Check presence, then have the student test the connection

After the student confirms key entry, you may run `python3 setup-key.py check`
(Windows: `py -3 setup-key.py check`). This prints only presence/missing status;
it does not read the key or prove authentication.

Have the student create a NEW empty local folder, open a normal terminal
there, and run `opencode`. Keep it outside any existing repository so project
config cannot override the course settings. In `/models`, verify DeepThought
and `ets:aws:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`. Ask OpenCode:
"Create hello.py that prints Hello CS 450, run it, and show the output."
Use `python` or `python3` as appropriate to the installed interpreter.
Success means the file exists AND ran with that output through DeepThought.
An installed executable, a model listing, or a chat reply is insufficient.

If 401/403: ask Matt to check key eligibility/validity; never ask to see the
key. For connection errors: check campus/VPN requirements with Matt; do not
disable TLS verification or change the endpoint. For an unsupported model or
schema: report exact OpenCode version and a redacted error category. Do not
switch providers or invent a replacement model. The old KB's recommendation
to run `opencode debug config` is intentionally excluded because it may reveal
the resolved key.

Report: OS/environment, OpenCode version, config prepared or conflict, key
presence only, and student-confirmed smoke-test result (or "not yet tested").
Never claim an authenticated test succeeded without the student's receipt.

## Sources

- [UNH OpenCode setup](https://td.usnh.edu/TDClient/60/Portal/KB/Article/5506/): DeepThought endpoint/model and OpenCode 1.x provider configuration, checked 2026-10-19.
- [OpenCode config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/): file references, precedence, and enabled providers, checked 2026-10-19.
- [OpenCode installation](https://opencode.ai/docs/): installation options.
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download): Node/npm prerequisite installer.
- [Python](https://www.python.org/downloads/): helper prerequisite installer.
- [llms.txt proposal](https://llmstxt.org/): agent-readable Markdown convention; this file is supplied explicitly to Cursor.

Course source: `planning/week-08/l13-your-own-benchmark/companions/activity.md`
relative to the Fall 2026 course directory. That checklist targets agate;
this handout intentionally targets the student's own computer at Matt's request.
Matt owns key creation. No student key or campus machine was used to validate
this bundle; live course connectivity and native Windows/macOS testing remain
to be confirmed before calling it classroom-tested.
